slice.question: Can the automatic attestation generated for an immutable GitHub release provide an independently retained, deletion-surviving, directly scheduled-Chat-readable monotonic witness without repository Administration permission, local CLI execution, webhook/external storage, hosted compute, external execution, manual attestation, finite monthly/trial/paid quota, or added cost?

sources.title: Immutable releases - GitHub Docs
sources.observed: Publishing an immutable release automatically generates a release attestation containing the release tag, commit SHA, and release assets; the release itself can still be deleted even though tag/assets are immutable while the release exists.

sources.title: Artifact attestations - GitHub Docs
sources.observed: For public repositories, GitHub artifact attestations use the Sigstore Public Good Instance, store a copy of the Sigstore bundle with GitHub, and write it to an immutable transparency log that is publicly readable; private repositories use a GitHub Sigstore instance without a transparency log.

sources.title: REST API endpoints for artifact attestations - GitHub Docs
sources.observed: The artifact-attestation API supports predicate_type=release and public-resource attestation listing without authentication, but listing attestations requires a subject digest; the documentation does not establish repository+deleted-release-tag lookup of a release attestation.

sources.title: Security Model - Sigstore
sources.observed: A Rekor entry is designed as long-term evidence whose log contents cannot later be removed or tampered with.

sources.title: CLI - Sigstore
sources.observed: Rekor retrieval is documented by log index or UUID, and search is documented by artifact, public key, or SHA; no documented lookup by GitHub repository plus deleted release tag was found in this bounded slice.

sources.title: Sigstore Bundle Format - Sigstore
sources.observed: Transparency-log entries can be carried in bundles, but the generic bundle specification does not itself require them; GitHub's public artifact-attestation documentation provides the stronger product-specific logging statement.

reasoning: The reviewed GitHub documentation gives strong evidence that public artifact attestations are independently written to a public immutable transparency log, and the attestation REST surface recognizes a release predicate.

This supports a plausible deletion-surviving retention layer for public release attestations, but the bounded official documentation reviewed here does not explicitly prove that every automatically generated immutable-release attestation is written to that public log under the same guarantee.

More decisively, direct retrieval after release/tag deletion still requires a Rekor UUID/log index, an artifact/public-key/SHA search key, or a GitHub subject digest. The reviewed docs do not establish a way to derive one of those lookup keys solely from surviving repository identity plus the deleted release tag after the release assets/tag are gone.

Persisting that UUID/digest/hash in another store would itself be the external persistent-state dependency this child was required to avoid. Therefore the candidate cannot yet satisfy the complete monotonic rollback-witness route.
slice.tested_scope: Official public GitHub and Sigstore documentation only.
